root_cause.text: The ICE loopback VSI path did not allocate or initialize a `q_vector`/`napi` for `ICE_VSI_LB`, so after the Page Pool conversion `ice_vsi_cfg_rxq()`/`ice_rxq_pp_create()` dereferenced a NULL `ring->q_vector`/`napi` while setting up the RX ring during the offline ethtool loopback test.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says “It crashes because we have not initialized libeth for the rx ring” and that the fix is to “lett[ing] them have a q_vector… [with] a napi struct that can be passed to libeth_rx_fq_create() called from ice_vsi_cfg_rxq() -> ice_rxq_pp_create().” The diff shows `ICE_VSI_LB` previously skipped q_vector allocation (`if (vsi->type == ICE_VSI_LB) return 0;` was removed), `ice_vsi_set_num_qs()` now sets `vsi->num_q_vectors = 1` for LB, and `ice_vsi_cfg_def()` allocates/mapps a dummy q_vector to `rx_rings[0]`, confirming the crash came from missing q_vector/napi initialization for loopback RX rings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip q_vector allocation for loopback VSIs by routing ICE_VSI_LB entries to the existing skip_alloc path.
intent_record.what: In ice_vsi_alloc_q_vector(), a new conditional branch was added for VSI type ICE_VSI_LB that jumps to the existing skip_alloc label, placing it before the ICE_VSI_CTRL && vsi->vf branch.
intent_record.how: For loopback VSIs, the function now bypasses q_vector allocation entirely instead of proceeding through the normal allocation path, preventing allocation work that should not occur for this VSI type.

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable XDP RX queue registration for ICE loopback VSI rings by including ICE_VSI_LB in the existing type check.
intent_record.what: The conditional in `ice_vsi_cfg_rxq()` was expanded so that the `xdp_rxq_info` registration path now also runs when `ring->vsi->type == ICE_VSI_LB`, in addition to the existing `ICE_VSI_PF` and `ICE_VSI_SF` cases.
intent_record.how: At runtime, loopback VSI receive rings will now be treated like PF and SF rings for XDP RX queue registration, allowing the XDP RX queue metadata to be set up for that VSI type instead of skipping it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the test ring's NAPI device pointer so loopback setup can successfully create the RX queue pair.
intent_record.what: The code adds an assignment in `ice_loopback_test()` that sets `rx_ring->q_vector->napi.dev = netdev;` and includes a comment explaining that only the minimum required dummy `q_vector` and `napi` fields are being filled for `ice_rxq_pp_create()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the loopback test now initializes the `napi.dev` pointer for the receive ring's q_vector before ring preparation, which allows `ice_rxq_pp_create()` to access the expected device context instead of operating on an uninitialized field and potentially failing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allocate q_vectors for loopback VSIs by removing the special-case early return.
intent_record.what: The code removes the early return that skipped q_vector allocation when `vsi->type == ICE_VSI_LB`, so `ice_vsi_alloc_arrays()` will now continue past that check and allocate `vsi->q_vectors` for loopback VSIs as well.
intent_record.how: At runtime, loopback VSI instances will no longer bypass q_vector array allocation. This changes initialization behavior so loopback VSIs are treated like other VSI types in this allocation path, which can prevent later code from encountering missing q_vector storage for loopback configurations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure loopback VSIs get a dummy q_vector by setting num_q_vectors to 1.
intent_record.what: In the ICE_VSI_LB case inside ice_vsi_set_num_qs(), two new lines were added: a comment stating "A dummy q_vector, no actual IRQ." and an assignment setting vsi->num_q_vectors = 1.
intent_record.how: For loopback VSIs, the code now explicitly allocates one q_vector even though no real interrupt is used. This ensures the VSI has the expected q_vector structure/state for downstream logic that may assume at least one q_vector exists.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix loopback VSI initialization by allocating and wiring a q_vector before rings are created and mapping the dummy RX ring to it.
intent_record.what: In the ICE_VSI_LB case of ice_vsi_cfg_def(), the code now allocates q_vectors before allocating rings, adds error handling to unwind q_vector allocation if ring allocation fails, and assigns the first q_vector to the only rx_ring via vsi->rx_rings[0]->q_vector = vsi->q_vectors[0].
intent_record.how: This changes loopback VSI initialization so a q_vector exists before ring setup and the dummy receive ring is explicitly associated with that q_vector. It prevents ring setup from proceeding without the required q_vector and ensures the loopback path has a valid ring-to-vector mapping.

    This patch adds a handler for ethtool selftest. Selftest includes

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff for this commit shows explicit loopback-VSI handling that avoids the missing q_vector/NAPI setup described in the root cause. In particular, `ice_vsi_alloc_arrays()` now returns early for `ICE_VSI_LB` with `/* There is no need to allocate q_vectors for a loopback VSI. */ if (vsi->type == ICE_VSI_LB) return 0;`, and `ice_vsi_setup()` adds `case ICE_VSI_LB: ret = ice_vsi_alloc_rings(vsi); ... break;`, so loopback VSIs are set up differently instead of following the PF path that expects q_vectors. The bug-triggering pattern of dereferencing an absent q_vector is also guarded later in `ice_vsi_stop_tx_rings()` by changing `if (!rings || !rings[q_idx] || !rings[q_idx]->q_vector)` to `if (!rings || !rings[q_idx])` and then only triggering the interrupt when `if (rings[q_idx]->q_vector) { ... }`. Because this commit adds the special handling needed for `ICE_VSI_LB`, the vulnerable construct is not present in this version and the fix is already in place.
